SPECIFICATION FO-R 90 mm FLEXIBLE DISK CARTRIDGE USING MODIFIED FREQUENCY RECORDING AT 7 958 ftprad ON 80 TRACKS ON EACH SIDE
PART NATIONAL FOREWORD 2 TRACK FORMAT

This Indian Standard ( Part 2 ), which is identical with IS0 8860-2 : 1987 `Information processing - Data interchange on 90 mm ( 3% in ) flexible disk cartridges using modified frequency modulation recording at 7 958 ftprad on 80 tracks on each side - Part 2 : Track format', issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 15 December 1989 on the recommendations of the Computers, Business Machines and Calculators Sectional Committee ( LTD 24 ) and approval of the Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council. The text of the IS0 standard has been approved as suitable for publication as Indian Standard without deviations. Certain conventions are, however, not identical with those used in Indian Standards. Attention is particularly drawn to the following: a) Wherever the words `International Standard' appear, referring to this standard, they should be read as `Indian Standard'. b) c) Comma ( , J has been used as a decimal marker while in Indian Standards the current practice is to use a-point ( . ) as the decimal marker. For the purpose of this Indian Standard, metric dimensions shall be applicable.

Introduction

IS0 8860-1, information processing - Data interchange on 90 mm (3.5 in) flexible disk cartridges using modified frequency
modulation side teristics. Part recording 1 at 7 958 ftprad on 80 tracks on each physical and magnetic charac-

IS0 9960 specifies the characteristics of 90 mm (3.5 in) flexible disk cartridges recorded at 7 959 ftprad using Modified Frequency Modulation (MFM) recording on 80 tracks on each side. IS0 8860-l specifies the mechanical, physical and magnetic characteristics of the cartridga, so as to provide physical interchangeability between data processing systems. IS0 8860-l and IS0 88602, together with the labelling scheme specified in IS0 9293, provide for full data interchange between data processing systems.

This part of IS0 8860 specifies the track layout, the track format and the characteristics of recorded signals.
NOTE - Numeric values in the SI and/or Imperial measurement system in this part of IS0 8860 may have been rounded off and therefore are consistent with, abut not exactly equal to, each other. Either system may be used, but the two should be neither intermixed nor re-converted. The original design was made using St units.

The mode of recording shall be Modified Frequency Modulation (MFM) for which the conditions are a) a flux transition shall be written at the centre of each bit cell containing a ONE; b) a flux transition shall be written at each cell boundary between consecutive bit cells containing ZEROS. Exceptions to this are defined in 4.12.

Track location tolerance flexible disk cartridge of the recorded

A 90 mm (3.5 in) flexible disk cartridge shall be in conformance with this part of IS0 8860 if it meets all mandatory requirements contained herein. A prerequisite for conformance with this part of IS0 8890 is conformance with IS0 8860-l.

The centrelines of the recorded tracks shall be within + 0,028mm ( k 0.001 1 in) of the nominal positions and over the range of operating environment specified in IS0 8860-l.

The instantaneous spacing between flux transitions is influenced by the reading and writing process, the bit sequence (pulse crowding effects) and other factors. The locations of the transitions are defined as the locations of the peaks in the signal when reading. Tests should be carried out using a peak-sensing amplifier (see annexes I3 and Cl.

Figure 1

4.5.1 The-spacing between the flux transitions in a sequence of ONES shall be between 80 % and 120 % of the short-term average bit cell length.

NOTE - As tracks may be written and overwritten at extremes of the tolerances given in 4.2 and 4.3, a band of old information may be left at one edge of the newly written data and would constitute unwanted noise when reading. It is, therefore, necessary to trim the edges of the tracks by erasure after writing.

4.5.2 The spacing between the flux transition for a ONE and that between two ZEROS preceding or following it shall be between 130 % and 165 % ot the short-term average bit cell length.

The nominal density of recording shall be 7 958 ftprad. The resulting nominal bit cell length is 125,7 prad.

Track layout

The cylinder number shall be a two-digit number identical with the track number of the tracks of the cylinder. 4.11 Data capacity of a track

After formatting, there shall be 9 sectors on each track. The layout of each track shall be as shown in figure 3. 5.1 Index

Gap

The data capacity of a track shall be 4 608 bytes. 4:12 Hexadecimal notation

At nominal density, this field shall comprise not less than 32 bytes and not more than 146 bytes of unspecified content [but not containing any (Al)`-bytes]. Writing the Index Gap is started when the index is detected. The index in any track lies on a line that is parallel to radius 6 in figure 4 of IS0 8860-I and spaced 0,36 mm (0.014 in) from it. Any of the first 16 bytes may be ill-defined due to overwriting. 5.2 Sector Identifier

5.2.2

Data Mark

This field shall comprise 6 bytes.

This field shall comprise 16 bytes: 12 KMl)-bytes 3 (Al)*-bytes 1 (FBI-byte 5.4.2 Data Field

5.2.2.1

Track Address

This field shall comprise 2 bytes : a) Cylinder Number (C)

This field shall specify in binary notation the cylinder number from 00 for the outermost cylinder to 79 for the innermost cylinder. b) Side Number (side)

This field shall comprise 512 bytes. If it comprises less than the requisite number of data bytes, the remaining positions shall be filled with UlO)-bytes. 5.4.3 EDC

This field shall specify the side of the disk. On side 0, it shall be (00) on all tracks. On Side 1 it shall be (01) on all tracks.

These two bytes shall be generated as defined in 4.13 using the bytes of the Data Block starting with the first (Al )*-byte of the Data Mark and ending with the last byte of the Data Field. If the EDC is incorrect, then the sector is defective. IS0 9293 specifies the handling of defective sectors.

5.2.2.2

Sector Number (S)

.

The 3rd byte shall specify in binary notation the sector number from 01 for the first sector to 09 for the last sector. The sectors may be recorded in any order of their sector numbers.

5.5

Data Block Gap

This field shall comprise initially not less than 78 bytes and not more than 84 (4ELbytes. These bytes may have become illdefined due to overwriting. The Data Block Gap is recorded after each Data Block and it precedes the following Sector Identifier. After the last Data Block, it precedes the Track Gap.

5.2.2.3

4th byte

5.6
The 4th byte shall always be a (02Lbyte.

Track Gap

5.2.2.4

EDC

This field shall follow the Data Block Gap of the last sector. (4ELbytes are written until the index is detected, unless it has been detected during writing of the last Data Block Gap, in which case there shall be no Track Gap.

These two bytes shall be generated as defined in 4.13 using the bytes of the Sector Identifier starting with the first (Al)*-byte (see 5.2.1) of the Identifier Mark and ending with the 4th byte (see 5.2.2.3) of the Address Identifier. tf the EDC is incorrect, then the sector is defective. IS0 9293 specifies the handling of defective sectors.

The contents of the data field shall be recorded and interpreted according to the relevant lnternaticinal Standards for the coding of information, for example IS0 646, IS0 2022 or IS0 4873.

5.3

Identifier

Gap 8.2 Coding methods

This field shall comprise initially 22 (4E)-bytes. These bytes may have become ill-defined due to overwriting.

6.2.1 When the coding method requires it, the data field shall be regarded as an ordered sequence of 8-bit bytes. Within each byte the bit positions shall be identified by B8 to Bl .The high-order bit shall be recorded in position B8 and the low-order bit in position Bl .The sequence of recording shall be high-order bit first.

Annex Procedure and equipment

B flux transition spacing

for measuring

(This annex does not form part of the standard.)

B.l

General

This annex specifies an equipment and a procedure for measuring flux transition spacing on 90 mm flexible disk cartridges using MFM recording at 7 958 flux transitions per radian Utprad) on each side. The text is written for use when testing at a nominal rotational speed of 600 r/min. When the nominal speed of test is 300 r/min, the requirements, when different, are given in parentheses.

B.2

Format

The disk to be measured shall be written by the disk drive for data interchange use. The test patterns 11011011 (DB) and 11011100 (DC) shall be written repeatedly on all tracks.

B.3
B.3.1

Test equipment
Disk drive

The disk drive shall have a rotational speed of 600 It 6 r/min (300 f. 3 r/min) averaged over one revolution. The average angular speed taken over 32 p.s (64 us) shall not deviate by more than 0,5 % from the speed averaged over one revolution.

8.3.2 8.3.2.1

Head Resolution

The head shall have an absolute resolution of 65 % to 75 % at track 79 on each side, using the Reference Material RM 8860, applying the calibration factor of the Reference Material appropriate to the side, and recording with the appropriate Test Recording Current. The resonant frequency of the head shall be at least 500 000 Hz (250 000 Hz). The resolution shall not be adjusted by varying the load impedance of the head. The resolution shall be measured at the output of the amplifier defined in 8.3.3.1. B.3.2.2 Offset angle

The offset angle of the head shall be 8 = arc sin 0 d F f 6'

"

where d = 0.35 mm (0.014 in). B.3.2.3 Contact

Care shall be taken that the heads are in good contact with the disk &ring tests.

2t

The data separator should be capable of resolving a difference of 2 ps (at a rotational speed of 600 r/min). To achieve this with a low error rate, the data separator cannot operate on a fixed period but should follow changes in the bit cell length. It is recognized analogue that various techniques may be developed to achieve dynamic data separation; reliability. with present technology only an

data separator

baaed on a phase-locked

oscillator can provide the necessary
